metadata.title: Multigraph Sampling of Online Social Networks

extraction_notes.note: The prose description of the two-stage neighbor selection just before Algorithm 1 ('First, we select... Second, we pick...') restates the pseudocode, so it got no separate node; the equivalence sentence after it is ClP2.

Most of Sections 3-4 are experimental results read off figures and tables (Gelman-Rubin plots, isolate percentages, weekly charts); only a few headline empirical claims were emitted, as numerical-rigor claims.
remark or external theorem: the cited link between lambda_2 and mixing time is stated only qualitatively, so it is kept as an external remark.
remark or claim plus external theorem: the paragraph computes p*, cites the ER connectivity threshold and concludes intuitively in one go, so it is one remark rather than separate nodes.

The \label{alg:mixture} sits after \end{algorithmic}, so the finishing step did not tie it to the algorithm node; the uses edges from AP3 for each \ref{alg:mixture} were added by hand at confidence 0.9.
The algorithm steps of these prose procedures are sub-sentence spans (one operation each) inside a single sentence.

nodes.statement: Note that in Step~3, Algorithm~ requires only the values of degrees~d_i(v) of all relation graphs. Only in Step~4 of Algorithm~ does one enumerate all neighboring edges in the selected~G_i. nodes.statement: Let d(v,u)=d(u,v) be the number of edges between nodes v and u in the union multigraph G. The sampling process of Algorithm~ is a Markov chain on V with transition probabilities P_vu=fracd(v,u)d(v), u,v in V. So long as G is finite and connected, this random walk is irreducible and positive recurrent. The presence of a triangle within G further guarantees aperiodicity. A Markov chain of this type is equivalent to a random walk on an undirected weighted graph with edge weights w(v,u)=d(v,u). A random walk on weighted graph is known to have the unique equilibrium distribution pi(v)=fracw(v)sum_uin V w(u), where w(v)=sum_u w(v,u) (e.g., see ), and the proof follows immediately by substitution.
nodes.raw_latex:
Let $d(v,u)=d(u,v)$ be the number of edges between nodes $v$ and $u$ in the union multigraph $G$.
The sampling process of Algorithm~\ref{alg:mixture} is a Markov chain on $V$ with transition probabilities $P_{vu}=\frac{d(v,u)}{d(v)}, u,v \in V$.  So long as $G$ is finite and connected,
this random walk is irreducible and positive recurrent. The presence of a triangle within $G$ further guarantees aperiodicity.








A Markov chain of this type is equivalent to a random walk on an undirected weighted graph with edge weights $w(v,u)=d(v,u)$.
A random walk on weighted graph is known to have the unique equilibrium distribution
$\pi(v)=\frac{w(v)}{\sum_{u\in V} w(u)}$, where  $w(v)=\sum_{u} w(v,u)$
({\em e.g., } see \cite[Example 4.32]{RossBook}), and the proof follows immediately by substitution.

nodes.statement: Note that this example illustrates a more general phenomenon. Given Q independent random graphs with N nodes each and with expected densities p_1,ldots,p_Q, the probability that an edge \u,v\ belongs to their union graph G' is p^*=1-prod_i=1^Q(1-p_i). For p_i approximately equal, this approaches~1 exponentially fast in Q. Asymptotically, the union graph will be almost surely connected where (N-1) p^*> ln N , in which case the union multigraph is also trivially connected. Thus, intuitively, a relatively small number of sparse graphs are needed for the union to exceed its connectivity threshold.
nodes.raw_latex: Note that this example illustrates a more general phenomenon.  Given $Q$ independent random graphs with $N$ nodes each and with expected densities $p_1,\ldots,p_Q$, the probability that an edge $\{u,v\}$ belongs to their union graph $G'$ is $p^*=1-\prod_{i=1}^Q(1-p_i)$.  For $p_i$ approximately equal, this approaches~1 exponentially fast in $Q$.  Asymptotically, the union graph will be almost surely connected where $(N-1) p^*> \ln N$ \cite[pp413--417]{West96}, in which case the union multigraph is also trivially connected.  Thus, intuitively, a relatively small number of sparse graphs are needed for the union to exceed its connectivity threshold.
nodes.clean_text: Note that this example illustrates a more general phenomenon. Given Q independent random graphs with N nodes each and with expected densities p_1,ldots,p_Q, the probability that an edge \u,v\ belongs to their union graph G' is p^*=1-prod_i=1^Q(1-p_i). For p_i approximately equal, this approaches~1 exponentially fast in Q. Asymptotically, the union graph will be almost surely connected where (N-1) p^*> ln N , in which case the union multigraph is also trivially connected. Thus, intuitively, a relatively small number of sparse graphs are needed for the union to exceed its connectivity threshold.

nodes.statement: Although UNI sampling currently solves the problem of uniform node sampling in tt Last.fmxspace and is a valuable asset for this study, it is not a general solution for sampling OSNs. Such an operation is not generally supported by OSNs. Furthermore, the userID space must not be sparse for this operation to be efficient. In the tt Last.fmxspace case, the small userID space makes this possible at the time of this writing; however, a simple increase of the userID space to 48 or 64 bits would render the technique infeasible. In summary, we were able to obtain a uniform sampling of userIDs and use it as a baseline for evaluating the sampling methods of interest against the target distribution.
